text:
Registered sales volume declined to 10,195 units in the last four weeks, representing a 6.1% drop from the previous period. The total transaction value reached AED 27,672,330,524, which is a 1.3% decrease compared to the prior four weeks. Mortgage registrations stood at 4,054, operating as a separate registration category distinct from sales transactions.

The median residential price per square foot fell to AED 1,666, marking an 1.8% reduction from the previous four weeks. Off-plan transactions accounted for 59.4% of the total sales volume. This share is lower than the 66.6% recorded in the preceding period, indicating a shift in the composition of registered transactions.

Rental activity remained robust with 92,512 Ejari contracts registered. Renewals constituted 50.2% of these contracts. The median residential rent was AED 70,000 per year. In terms of yields, Zaabeel First offered the highest estimated gross yield at 9.3% for flats, followed by International City Phase 1 at 8.6%.

The watch list highlights Al Yufrah 1 with a 36.5% increase in median price per square foot over 12 weeks. Conversely, Palm Jumeirah saw a 17.5% decline in the same metric. Dubai South led sales volume with 3,830 transactions in the last 12 weeks. The anomaly monitor flagged 1,025 sales in the last 60 days that deviated significantly from comparable medians.

Figures are derived from registered DLD data and Ejari contracts, using medians and benchmark filters that exclude bulk deals, partial shares, and statistical outliers.

facts.ranking_rule: communities with at least 30 eligible sales in both 12-week windows; yields also need 30 rent contracts of the same property type
